system_prompt:
You are agent_4, and the planning discussion is over.
Write the Swarmish document the next team will use. They will not see the chat, only this document.
Write it in ordinary English, not JSON, and include every convention needed to say something in
Swarmish.
The task team's messages may ONLY contain these glyphs, spaces, and agent IDs:
  r p g q t h m w 1 8 v i 6 2 7 y e o a j l 3 d 4 5 c f x z b u s 9 n 0 k
Each agent sees that list in its own order. Anything else they send is replaced with "⊘".

LANGUAGE REQUIREMENTS
- A fresh agent must be able to read and write Swarmish correctly from swarmish.txt alone.
- Meaning must come from what glyphs and combinations of glyphs stand for, as written in
  swarmish.txt, not from a procedure. Forbidden: any rule defined over the letters or spelling
  of English or any other natural language; spelling words out glyph by letter; any rule that
  requires arithmetic, counting positions, shifting, or any other calculation to read or write
  a message; any numerical representations based on binary, ASCII, Unicode, etc.
  If a round 2 agent would have to compute instead of look up or follow lexical rules, the procedure is not
  allowed. Please keep to the spirit of the game, which is language development based on meaning and not arithmetic.
- Keep swarmish.txt under 500 lines. Every round 2 agent reads all of it on every turn.
How you organize swarmish.txt beyond that is up to your team.
prompt:
CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH: COMPLETE REFERENCE
Purpose: communicate arbitrary task meanings using semantic words and lexical grammar. Every Swarmish message must contain only the permitted lowercase glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs. No punctuation, English, digit-spelling, transliteration, encoding, calculations, or letter-based transformations. The words below are arbitrary whole-meaning lexical entries, not a cipher algorithm. Read by lookup and grammatical composition.
Use this reference silently. Never give English glosses, bilingual examples, language lessons, or redundant alternate encodings in chat. Communicate task substance. Do not systematically restate a proposition in different vocabulary. Avoid predictable greetings and signatures. Security must not prevent accurate collaboration.
Every listed word is indivisible. Prefixes, suffixes, and similar spellings have NO productive meaning. Only the forms actually in THIS document exist; no earlier planning vocabulary applies.

GRAMMAR
Words are separated by spaces. A message may contain several complete sentences. All structural words below are reserved. Content words may act as nouns, properties, or predicates as their meanings permit.
A clause is: MOOD optionally NEGATION then PREDICATE then zero or more ROLE ARGUMENT pairs then ke.
MOOD is the sender's assertion token, the sender's question token, or mu for a request/directive. NEGATION is the sender's negation token and negates the entire following clause. PREDICATE is one content word. Each role takes exactly one argument. Roles may be in any order; omitted roles are understood from context, never silently reversed. Do not omit a role if ambiguity would matter.
Sender-specific lexicon: columns are ACTOR, THEME, QUESTION, NEGATION, ASSERTION. The repeated forms have genuinely different lexical meanings for different senders. Consult the printed row directly; there is no transformation rule.
agent_0: zavu kime rupq hedo falx
agent_1: rupq hedo falx kime zavu
agent_2: falx rupq hedo zavu kime
agent_3: hedo falx kime rupq zavu
agent_4: kime zavu falx hedo rupq
agent_5: rupq falx zavu kime hedo
agent_6: falx hedo kime zavu rupq
agent_7: hedo rupq zavu falx kime
Always consult the actual chat sender's row, including inside nested clauses or reported speech. These are separate lexical meanings, not substitutions to calculate. ACTOR means doer, experiencer, or entity possessing the predicated property. THEME means object, content, affected thing, or second participant.
Other roles, same for every sender: ri recipient/beneficiary; ta location; we time; so reference/standard/source; nu quantity/degree; yi manner/instrument; pu owner/possessor; ga purpose/goal. The English gloss of the predicate decides the natural interpretation of each role. For a property such as red, ACTOR is the red entity. For contain, ACTOR is container and THEME is contents. For greater-than, ACTOR is larger and THEME is smaller. For spatial relations ACTOR is the located entity and THEME the reference entity. A category noun used as a predicate means ACTOR is an instance of that category; thus object as predicate classifies ACTOR as an object.
ke closes exactly the current clause. Nested clauses are permitted as arguments; each has its own mood and ke. A nested clause denotes its proposition, so know, deny, ask, require, believe, and similar predicates can take propositions as THEME. Assertion mood inside an argument forms a proposition; it does not independently endorse it. mu requests that its clause be made true.
A question mood asks whether its clause is true unless an unknown argument is supplied. Unknown arguments ask for their satisfying values; multiple unknowns request jointly satisfying values. qi is an unrestricted unknown; the n-prefixed unknown words specify the requested semantic type.
A bare content word or agent ID is an argument. Agent IDs denote the corresponding agents, never their spelling. me denotes the current sender; tu denotes the current addressee if uniquely clear; sa denotes the whole team; ne is the bound referent used in descriptions; vu denotes the salient previously discussed entity/proposition; qi is an unknown requested argument.
fo followed by one or more content words or already bound handles and then lu is a descriptive noun phrase: the uniquely identifiable entity satisfying all listed meanings. For example a phrase combining object, red, small means the small red object. These are semantic modifiers, not a sequence encoding letters. Use only compatible meanings; use a relational description for richer structure. A numeral in this phrase is a quantity property, never a digit or ordinal. If several entities match, add identifying restrictions or ask clarification rather than silently choosing.
bi followed by one complete clause and then lu means the unique entity for which that clause holds, with ne standing for that entity. The clause must contain ne as an argument. Such descriptions may nest; ne binds to the innermost surrounding bi. Proposition nesting does NOT change this binding. Use a handle instead when nested reference would be confusing. If uniqueness is unavailable, clarify or use the quantified construction below.
ha HANDLE ARGUMENT ke is a naming sentence: publicly bind HANDLE to the referent of ARGUMENT. An argument can be an entity or a whole proposition. A handle subsequently denotes that referent without reconstructing the description. Check existing bindings first; do not silently rebind. Use a new handle for a corrected referent, and explicitly retract the erroneous claim.
Available initially unbound handles: doq dex dum diz daf dyv dok duf dav dem duq dez dym dif daq dov den duz div dal deq dymu davi doze dufe daxo duvi dema dyqo doli.
If these are exhausted, introduce another unused allowed-glyph word with ha; it must not be a dictionary or structural word. Its shape is arbitrary and unrelated to any external name, spelling, numeral, or encoded information. Naming binds a referent, not an English word. Bindings persist across speakers.
For unfamiliar task names, refer by semantic description, task-visible location, owner, category, or previously grounded handle. You may bind the entity shown at a described row or position. Never translate a name letter by letter. An ungrounded nickname cannot communicate a private unfamiliar name: provide its identifying semantic facts instead.
Use nested propositions for logical connection: a logical predicate takes ACTOR as one proposition and THEME as another. Thus if relates condition to consequence; because relates result to reason; before relates earlier event to later event; and means both propositions hold; or means at least one holds. For unary temporal/modal meanings, THEME is the modified proposition. Clause scope is always lexical and explicit.
Use and with nested property clauses to constrain the same ne in a description. This permits arbitrary conjunctions of color, ownership, location, and ordinal constraints. Deeper and clauses permit further conjuncts.
Use report with ACTOR as original speaker and THEME as proposition, but continue using the actual current sender's structural table. Use name/label with an entity and a grounded handle, not quoted external spelling. To discuss a previous claim use vu only if uniquely salient; otherwise bind its whole clause to a handle.
Counting construction: bo QUANTIFIER NUMBER bi CLAUSE lu ke is a complete sentence asserting that the number of ALL distinct entities satisfying CLAUSE with ne bound to each entity meets QUANTIFIER NUMBER. QUANTIFIER is x4vo exactly, xy2m at least, x8sc at most, x3hk more than, or xd6p less than. NUMBER is one directly listed cardinal quantity. Here bi is a restriction over all matching entities, NOT a demand that only one entity match. This is a semantic quantifier, not an instruction to encode or calculate. It constrains the entire matching set, never an arbitrary subset. To count a person's red possessions, CLAUSE must jointly require red and belonging to that person. To negate or question a count, use an ordinary negated/question clause with zif as predicate and the whole bo sentence as THEME; a bo sentence is also allowed as a proposition argument.
All/every and some may be used as predicates with ACTOR a bi description and THEME a proposition containing ne: all means every entity satisfying the description satisfies that proposition; some means at least one does; none means no entity does. In this special construction the ACTOR bi is a restriction over all matches, not a uniqueness claim, and ne in THEME refers to each quantified entity. Avoid nested descriptions there; bind other referents first.
There is no hidden omission convention, positional numerical notation, arithmetic code, or natural-language spelling rule. Do not invent one. Novel meanings must be composed from the semantic lexicon and descriptions. Ask for clarification rather than guessing.

USE AND REPAIR
Express essential facts first, then coordination and questions. Use precise explicit roles and grounded handles when mistakes would affect the task. A property can be predicated of an object; a proposition can be believed, negated, requested, compared, or assigned a confidence. Never confuse content zax with question mood, zur with assertion mood, or zev correct with spatial zoi right.
When information is private, identify its owner or source with pu or so and predicate zahm. When it becomes shared, state zux or send/share it. Different claims can be simultaneously reported without endorsing them; use nested report or believe clauses.
For a proposed plan, assert a preference or commitment toward a nested action clause. For acceptance or refusal, use agree/disagree or deny with a clearly referenced proposal. For correction, identify the mistaken claim and then provide its replacement; do not merely send an unexplained negation.
Clarify by semantic descriptions and grounded names only. Finish by reporting completion or remaining uncertainty, not by explaining the language. Unknown exact names or numerical values must not be represented by spelling, positional digits, Unicode, ASCII, arithmetic, or any other calculated code.

SWARMISH: COMPLETE REFERENCE

PURPOSE AND MESSAGE ALPHABET
Swarmish communicates task meanings through semantic words and explicit grammar. This reference is written in English; task messages must be in Swarmish only.
Task messages may contain spaces, literal agent IDs, and only these glyphs:
r p g q t h m w 1 8 v i 6 2 7 y e o a j l 3 d 4 5 c f x z b u s 9 n 0 k
The literal agent IDs agent_0 through agent_7 are permitted references to those agents. Other punctuation, uppercase letters, and unlisted symbols are not permitted.
The words below are arbitrary whole-meaning lexical entries, not a cipher algorithm. Read by lookup and grammatical composition. Never use spelling, transliteration, digit assembly, numerical encoding, calculations, or letter-based transformations.
Use this reference silently. Do not send English glosses, bilingual examples, language lessons, or redundant alternate encodings. Communicate task substance. Do not systematically restate a proposition in different vocabulary. Avoid predictable greetings and signatures. Security must not prevent accurate collaboration.
Every listed word is indivisible. Prefixes, suffixes, and similar spellings have NO productive meaning. Only forms in THIS document exist, apart from newly grounded handles introduced under the naming rule. No earlier planning vocabulary applies.

GRAMMAR
Words are separated by spaces. A message may contain several complete sentences. All structural words below are reserved. Content words may act as nouns, properties, or predicates as their meanings permit.
A clause is: MOOD optionally NEGATION then PREDICATE then zero or more ROLE ARGUMENT pairs then ke.
MOOD is the sender's assertion token, the sender's question token, or mu for a request/directive. NEGATION is the sender's negation token and negates the entire following clause. PREDICATE is one content word. Each role takes exactly one argument. Roles may be in any order. Omitted roles are understood from context, never silently reversed. Do not omit a role if ambiguity would matter.
Sender-specific lexicon: columns are ACTOR, THEME, QUESTION, NEGATION, ASSERTION. The repeated forms have genuinely different lexical meanings for different senders. Consult the printed row directly; there is no transformation rule.
agent_0: zavu kime rupq hedo falx
agent_1: rupq hedo falx kime zavu
agent_2: falx rupq hedo zavu kime
agent_3: hedo falx kime rupq zavu
agent_4: kime zavu falx hedo rupq
agent_5: rupq falx zavu kime hedo
agent_6: falx hedo kime zavu rupq
agent_7: hedo rupq zavu falx kime
Always consult the actual chat sender's row, including inside nested clauses or reported speech. These are separate lexical meanings, not substitutions to calculate.
ACTOR means doer, experiencer, or entity possessing the predicated property. THEME means object, content, affected thing, or second participant.
Other roles, same for every sender: ri recipient/beneficiary; ta location; we time; so reference/standard/source; nu quantity/degree; yi manner/instrument; pu owner/possessor; ga purpose/goal.
The predicate's meaning decides the natural interpretation of each role. For a property such as red, ACTOR is the red entity. For contain, ACTOR is container and THEME is contents. For greater-than, ACTOR is larger and THEME is smaller. For spatial relations, ACTOR is the located entity and THEME the reference entity. A category noun used as a predicate means ACTOR is an instance of that category; thus object as predicate classifies ACTOR as an object.
ke closes exactly the current clause. Nested clauses are permitted as arguments; each has its own mood and ke. A nested clause denotes its proposition, so know, deny, ask, require, believe, and similar predicates can take propositions as THEME. Assertion mood inside an argument forms a proposition; it does not independently endorse it. mu requests that its clause be made true.
A question mood asks whether its clause is true unless an unknown argument is supplied. Unknown arguments ask for their satisfying values; multiple unknowns request jointly satisfying values. qi is an unrestricted unknown; the listed typed unknown words specify the requested semantic type.
A bare content word or agent ID is an argument. Agent IDs denote the corresponding agents, never their spelling.
me denotes the current sender; tu denotes the current addressee if uniquely clear; sa denotes the whole team; ne is the bound referent used in descriptions; vu denotes the salient previously discussed entity/proposition; qi is an unknown requested argument.

DESCRIPTIONS AND NAMING
fo followed by one or more content words or already bound handles and then lu is a descriptive noun phrase: the uniquely identifiable entity satisfying all listed meanings. A bound handle contributes identity with its referent. For example, a phrase combining object, red, small means the small red object. These are semantic modifiers, not a sequence encoding letters.
Use only compatible meanings; use a relational description for richer structure. A cardinal quantity in this phrase is a quantity property, never a digit or ordinal. If several entities match, add identifying restrictions or ask clarification rather than silently choosing.
bi followed by one complete clause and then lu means the unique entity for which that clause holds, with ne standing for that entity. The clause must contain ne as an argument. Such descriptions may nest; ne binds to the innermost surrounding bi. Proposition nesting does NOT change this binding. Use a handle instead when nested reference would be confusing.
Ordinary bi and fo require unique contextual identification. Counting and all/some/none constructions below explicitly override bi uniqueness and treat it as a restriction over potentially many matches.
ha HANDLE ARGUMENT ke is a naming sentence: publicly bind HANDLE to the referent of ARGUMENT. An argument can be an entity or a whole proposition. A handle subsequently denotes that referent without reconstructing the description.
Check existing bindings first; do not silently rebind. Use a new handle for a corrected referent, and explicitly retract the erroneous claim. Bindings persist across speakers.
Available initially unbound handles:
doq dex dum diz daf dyv dok duf dav dem duq dez dym dif daq dov den duz div dal deq dymu davi doze dufe daxo duvi dema dyqo doli
If these are exhausted, introduce another unused allowed-glyph word with ha; it must not be a dictionary or structural word. Its shape is arbitrary and unrelated to any external name, spelling, numeral, or encoded information. Naming binds a referent, not an English word.
For unfamiliar task names, refer by semantic description, task-visible location, owner, category, or previously grounded handle. You may bind the entity shown at a described row or position. Never translate a name letter by letter. An ungrounded nickname cannot communicate a private unfamiliar name: provide its identifying semantic facts instead.

LOGICAL COMPOSITION AND QUANTIFICATION
Use nested propositions for logical connection: a binary logical predicate takes ACTOR as one proposition and THEME as another.
v4vo if relates ACTOR condition to THEME consequence; v3hk because relates ACTOR result to THEME reason; vz1r before relates ACTOR earlier event to THEME later event; v5xn after relates ACTOR later event to THEME earlier event.
vafu and means both propositions hold; veb7 or means at least one holds; v9wi either-but-not-both means exactly one holds. vy2m consequence and vd6p therefore relate ACTOR premise/condition to THEME consequence. v8sc unless relates ACTOR exception to THEME proposition that holds if the exception does not hold.
For unary temporal/modal meanings, THEME is the modified proposition. Clause scope is always lexical and explicit.
Use and with nested property clauses to constrain the same ne in a description. This permits conjunctions of color, ownership, location, and ordinal constraints. Deeper and clauses permit further conjuncts.
Use report with ACTOR as original speaker and THEME as proposition, but continue using the actual current sender's structural table. Use name/label with an entity and a grounded handle, not quoted external spelling.
To discuss a previous claim use vu only if uniquely salient; otherwise bind its whole clause to a handle.
Counting construction: bo QUANTIFIER NUMBER bi CLAUSE lu ke is a complete sentence asserting that the number of ALL distinct entities satisfying CLAUSE with ne bound to each entity meets QUANTIFIER NUMBER.
QUANTIFIER is x4vo exactly, xy2m at least, x8sc at most, x3hk more than, or xd6p less than. NUMBER is one directly listed cardinal quantity.
Here bi is a restriction over all matching entities, NOT a demand that only one entity match. This is a semantic quantifier, not an instruction to encode or calculate. It constrains the entire matching set, never an arbitrary subset.
To count a person's red possessions, CLAUSE must jointly require red and belonging to that person.
To negate or question a count, use an ordinary negated/question clause with zif as predicate and the whole bo sentence as THEME. A bo sentence is also allowed as a proposition argument.
All/every, some, and none may be used as predicates with ACTOR a bi description and THEME a proposition containing ne: all means every entity satisfying the description satisfies that proposition; some means at least one does; none means no entity does.
In this special construction the ACTOR bi is a restriction over all matches, not a uniqueness claim, and ne in THEME refers to each quantified entity. Avoid nested descriptions there; bind other referents first.
There is no hidden omission convention, positional numerical notation, arithmetic code, or natural-language spelling rule. Do not invent one. Novel meanings must be composed from the semantic lexicon and descriptions. Ask for clarification rather than guessing.

REFERENCE AND RELATIONAL WORDS

For n7i ACTOR possesses THEME; for nya ACTOR belongs to THEME; for neo ACTOR has THEME property; for noa ACTOR is an instance/member of THEME kind/set. For comparisons ACTOR is compared to THEME in the stated direction.
For color as a relation, zaj means ACTOR has THEME as its color. Unary zta means ACTOR is red.
qyu has ordinal position: ACTOR entity, THEME directly listed ordinal. qze has cardinal quantity: ACTOR collection, THEME directly listed quantity. 7uf is a synonym of qze with exactly the same roles.
jpa occupies task-visible position: ACTOR item, THEME grounded ordinal or location; ta may specify its containing list/grid.

SWARMISH: COMPLETE REFERENCE

PURPOSE AND LIMITS
Swarmish communicates task meanings through semantic words and explicit grammar. Task messages may contain only spaces, literal agent IDs, and these glyphs:
e r b d o v 4 x h i 5 w j s g 7 c y 3 p m q 6 1 z u 9 n t 2 a k 8 f l 0
The displayed order of the glyphs has no meaning. Do not send punctuation or English in task messages. Other characters are replaced with ⊘.
This reference is written in English for learning the language; task messages must be in Swarmish.
Words are arbitrary whole-meaning lexical entries, not a cipher algorithm. Read by lookup and grammatical composition.
Every listed word is indivisible. Prefixes, suffixes, and similar spellings have NO productive meaning. Only forms in this document and properly introduced discourse handles exist. No earlier planning vocabulary applies.
No spelling, transliteration, digit assembly, natural-language letter rules, positional numerical codes, binary, ASCII, Unicode, shifting, arithmetic encoding, or other calculated representation is permitted.
Use this reference silently. Never send English glosses, bilingual demonstrations, language lessons, or redundant alternate encodings. Communicate task substance. Do not systematically restate a proposition in different vocabulary. Avoid predictable greetings and signatures. Security must not prevent accurate collaboration.

BASIC GRAMMAR
Words are separated by spaces. A message may contain several complete sentences. Structural words are reserved.
Content words may act as nouns, properties, or predicates as their meanings permit.
An ordinary clause has this form:
MOOD optionally NEGATION then PREDICATE then zero or more ROLE ARGUMENT pairs then ke
MOOD is the sender's assertion token, the sender's question token, or mu for a request/directive.
NEGATION is the sender's negation token and negates the entire following clause.
PREDICATE is one content word. Each role takes exactly one argument.
Roles may appear in any order. Omitted roles are understood from context, never silently reversed. Do not omit a role when ambiguity would matter.
ke closes exactly the current clause.
mu requests that its clause be made true.

SENDER-SPECIFIC STRUCTURAL LEXICON
Columns are ACTOR, THEME, QUESTION, NEGATION, ASSERTION.
The repeated forms have genuinely different lexical meanings for different senders. Consult the actual printed row directly; there is no transformation rule.
agent_0: zavu kime rupq hedo falx
agent_1: rupq hedo falx kime zavu
agent_2: falx rupq hedo zavu kime
agent_3: hedo falx kime rupq zavu
agent_4: kime zavu falx hedo rupq
agent_5: rupq falx zavu kime hedo
agent_6: falx hedo kime zavu rupq
agent_7: hedo rupq zavu falx kime
Always use the actual chat sender's row, including inside nested clauses and reported speech. Never switch to the reported speaker's row.
ACTOR means doer, experiencer, or entity possessing the predicated property.
THEME means object, content, affected thing, or second participant.
Other roles, identical for every sender:
ri recipient/beneficiary; ta location; we time; so reference/standard/source; nu quantity/degree; yi manner/instrument; pu owner/possessor; ga purpose/goal.
The predicate's meaning decides the natural interpretation of a role.
For a property such as red, ACTOR is the red entity.
For contain, ACTOR is the container and THEME its contents.
For greater-than, ACTOR is larger and THEME smaller.
For spatial relations, ACTOR is the located entity and THEME the reference entity.
A category noun used as a predicate means ACTOR is an instance of that category. Thus object as predicate classifies ACTOR as an object.
Binary predicates use ACTOR as subject and THEME as reference/object unless explicitly stated otherwise.

ARGUMENTS, QUESTIONS, AND PROPOSITIONS
A bare content word, agent ID, pronoun, or bound handle is an argument.
Agent IDs denote the corresponding agents, never their spelling.
me denotes the current sender; tu denotes the current addressee if uniquely clear; sa denotes the whole team.
ne is the bound referent used in descriptions.
vu denotes the salient previously discussed entity or proposition.
qi is an unrestricted unknown requested argument.
The typed unknown words in the reference lexicon specify the requested semantic type.
A question mood asks whether its clause is true unless an unknown argument is supplied.
An unknown argument asks for its satisfying value. Multiple unknown arguments request jointly satisfying values.
Nested clauses are permitted as arguments. Each has its own mood and ke.
A nested clause denotes its proposition. Know, deny, ask, require, believe, and similar predicates can take propositions as THEME.
Assertion mood inside an argument forms a proposition; it does not independently endorse it.
Do not confuse content zax, meaning question/inquiry, with question mood, or content zur, meaning assert/claim, with assertion mood.

DESCRIPTIONS
fo followed by one or more content words or already bound handles and then lu is a descriptive noun phrase.
It denotes the uniquely identifiable entity satisfying all listed meanings. A phrase combining object, red, and small means the small red object.
These are semantic modifiers, not a sequence encoding letters. Use only compatible meanings.
A cardinal quantity in a fo phrase is a quantity property, never a digit or ordinal.
Use a relational description for ownership, location, ordinal position, or other richer structure.
If several entities match, add restrictions or ask clarification rather than silently choosing.
bi followed by one complete clause and then lu denotes the unique entity for which that clause holds, with ne standing for that entity.
The clause must contain ne as an argument.
Descriptions may nest. ne binds to the innermost surrounding bi.
Proposition nesting does NOT change this binding. Only a nested description shadows it.
Use a handle when nested reference would otherwise be confusing.
Use and with nested property clauses to constrain the same ne. Deeper and clauses permit further constraints.
Ordinary bi and fo require unique contextual identification. The counting and all/some/none constructions below explicitly override bi uniqueness.

NAMING AND GROUNDING
ha HANDLE ARGUMENT ke is a complete naming sentence. It publicly binds HANDLE to the referent of ARGUMENT.
An argument can be an entity or a whole proposition.
A handle subsequently denotes that referent without reconstructing its description.
Bindings persist across speakers. Check existing bindings first; do not silently rebind.
Use a new handle for a corrected referent and explicitly retract the erroneous claim.
Available initially unbound handles:
doq dex dum diz daf dyv dok duf dav dem duq dez dym dif daq dov den duz div dal deq dymu davi doze dufe daxo duvi dema dyqo doli
If these are exhausted, introduce another unused allowed-glyph word with ha. It must not be a dictionary or structural word.
Its shape is arbitrary and unrelated to any external name, spelling, numeral, or encoded information.
Naming binds a referent, not an English word.
For unfamiliar task names, refer by semantic description, task-visible location, owner, category, or a previously grounded handle.
You may bind the entity shown at a described row or position.
Never translate a name letter by letter. An ungrounded nickname cannot communicate a private unfamiliar name; provide its identifying semantic facts instead.
Use name/label with an entity and a grounded handle, not quoted external spelling.

LOGICAL CONNECTIONS AND REPORTS
A binary logical predicate takes ACTOR as one proposition and THEME as another.
If relates ACTOR condition to THEME consequence.
Because relates ACTOR result to THEME reason.
Before relates ACTOR earlier event to THEME later event.
And means both propositions hold. Inclusive or means at least one holds. Either-but-not-both means exactly one holds.
For unary temporal/modal meanings, THEME is the modified proposition.
Clause scope is lexical and explicit.
Use report with ACTOR as original speaker and THEME as proposition, while continuing to use the actual current sender's structural row.
To discuss a previous claim, use vu only when uniquely salient; otherwise bind its whole clause to a handle.

COUNTING AND QUANTIFICATION
bo QUANTIFIER NUMBER bi CLAUSE lu ke is a complete counting sentence.
It asserts that the number of ALL distinct entities satisfying CLAUSE, with ne bound to each entity, meets QUANTIFIER NUMBER.
QUANTIFIER is x4vo exactly, xy2m at least, x8sc at most, x3hk more than, or xd6p less than.
NUMBER is one directly listed cardinal quantity.
Here bi supplies a restriction over all matching entities, NOT a unique-entity argument. Uniqueness is not required.
The count constrains the entire matching set, never an arbitrary subset.
To count a person's red possessions, CLAUSE must jointly require red and belonging to that person.
This is semantic quantification, not an instruction to encode or calculate.
A bo sentence may also be a proposition argument.
To negate or question a count, use an ordinary negated or question clause with zif as predicate and the whole bo sentence as THEME.
All/every, some, and none may be predicates with ACTOR a bi description and THEME a proposition containing ne.
All means every entity satisfying the restriction satisfies that proposition; some means at least one does; none means no entity does.
In this special construction, ACTOR bi is a restriction over all matches and is exempt from ordinary uniqueness.
ne in THEME refers to each quantified entity. Avoid nested descriptions there; bind other referents first.

This binds doq to the uniquely salient red item. The fo phrase combines item and red semantically.

This binds dex to the unique entity in second ordinal position. Supply ta with a grounded list when needed to make the position unique.

Express essential facts first, then coordination and questions.
Use explicit roles and grounded handles when mistakes would affect the task.
A property can be predicated of an object; a proposition can be believed, negated, requested, compared, or assigned a confidence.
When information is private, identify its owner or source with pu or so and predicate zahm.
When it becomes shared, state zux or send/share it.
Different claims can be reported without endorsing them; use nested report or believe clauses.
For a proposed plan, assert a preference or commitment toward a nested action clause.
For acceptance or refusal, use agree/disagree or deny with a clearly referenced proposal.
For correction, identify the mistaken claim and provide its replacement; do not send an unexplained negation.
Clarify by semantic descriptions and grounded names only.
If a description is ambiguous, add restrictions or ask clarification. Do not silently choose a referent.
Finish by reporting completion or remaining uncertainty, not by explaining the language.
There is no hidden omission convention, positional numerical notation, arithmetic code, natural-language spelling rule, or productive word-shape rule. Do not invent one.
Novel meanings must be composed from the semantic lexicon and descriptions.
Unknown exact names or numerical values must not be represented by spelling, positional digits, Unicode, ASCII, arithmetic, or another calculated code.
Ask for clarification rather than guessing.

GRAMMAR
Words are separated by spaces. A message may contain several complete sentences. All structural words below are reserved. Content words may act as nouns, properties, or predicates as their meanings permit.
A clause is: MOOD optionally NEGATION then PREDICATE then zero or more ROLE ARGUMENT pairs then ke.
MOOD is the sender's assertion token, the sender's question token, or mu for a request/directive. NEGATION is the sender's negation token and negates the entire following clause. PREDICATE is one content word. Each role takes exactly one argument. Roles may be in any order; omitted roles are understood from context, never silently reversed. Do not omit a role if ambiguity would matter.
Sender-specific lexicon: columns are ACTOR, THEME, QUESTION, NEGATION, ASSERTION. The repeated forms have genuinely different lexical meanings for different senders. Consult the printed row directly; there is no transformation rule.

agent_2: falx rupq hedo zavu kime

ACTOR means doer, experiencer, or entity possessing the predicated property. THEME means object, content, affected thing, or second participant.

The English gloss of the predicate decides the natural interpretation of each role. For a property such as red, ACTOR is the red entity. For contain, ACTOR is container and THEME is contents. For greater-than, ACTOR is larger and THEME is smaller. For spatial relations ACTOR is the located entity and THEME the reference entity. A category noun used as a predicate means ACTOR is an instance of that category; thus object as predicate classifies ACTOR as an object.
ke closes exactly the current clause. Nested clauses are permitted as arguments; each has its own mood and ke. A nested clause denotes its proposition, so know, deny, ask, require, believe, and similar predicates can take propositions as THEME. Assertion mood inside an argument forms a proposition; it does not independently endorse it. mu requests that its clause be made true.

SWARMISH: COMPLETE REFERENCE

PURPOSE AND MESSAGE RULES
Swarmish communicates task meanings through whole-meaning words and explicit grammar. This document is the complete reference; no earlier planning vocabulary applies.
Task messages may contain only spaces, literal agent IDs, and these glyphs:
z c 0 s l b q e 3 9 k o 2 y u g i 7 8 t a n p 5 m h 1 r 4 f v x d w 6 j
The displayed order of those glyphs has no significance. Do not send punctuation, uppercase letters, English glosses, or other characters.
All vocabulary forms below are indivisible lexical entries. Shared prefixes, suffixes, or similar spellings have NO productive meaning. Read words by lookup, never by calculation or transformation.
Do not spell external words glyph by glyph, transliterate names, concatenate digits, encode natural-language spelling, or use binary, ASCII, Unicode, arithmetic, shifting, positions within a glyph list, or any other calculated code.
Use this reference silently. Communicate task substance, not language lessons, bilingual examples, redundant alternate encodings, predictable greetings, or signatures. Do not systematically restate propositions in different vocabulary. These economy rules must not prevent accurate collaboration.

GRAMMAR
Words are separated by spaces. A message may contain several complete sentences. Structural words are reserved. Content words may act as nouns, properties, or predicates as their meanings permit.
An ordinary clause has this form:
MOOD optionally NEGATION then PREDICATE then zero or more ROLE ARGUMENT pairs then ke
MOOD is the actual sender's assertion token, the actual sender's question token, or mu for a request/directive.
NEGATION is the actual sender's negation token. It negates the entire following clause.
PREDICATE is one content word. Each role takes exactly one argument. Roles may occur in any order. Omitted roles are understood from context, never silently reversed. Do not omit a role when ambiguity would matter.

SENDER-SPECIFIC STRUCTURAL LEXICON
Columns are ACTOR, THEME, QUESTION, NEGATION, ASSERTION.

agent_1: rupq hedo falx kime zavu
agent_2: falx rupq hedo zavu kime
agent_3: hedo falx kime rupq zavu
agent_4: kime zavu falx hedo rupq
agent_5: rupq falx zavu kime hedo

These rows are independent lexical lookups, not a transformation rule. Repeated forms genuinely have different meanings for different senders.
Always use the actual chat sender's row throughout the message, including nested clauses and reported speech. Never switch to a reported speaker's row.
ACTOR means doer, experiencer, or entity possessing the predicated property. THEME means object, content, affected thing, or second participant.
Other roles are the same for every sender:
ri recipient/beneficiary; ta location; we time; so reference/standard/source; nu quantity/degree; yi manner/instrument; pu owner/possessor; ga purpose/goal.
The predicate's meaning determines the natural interpretation of its roles. For contain, ACTOR is container and THEME is contents. For greater-than, ACTOR is larger and THEME is smaller. For spatial relations, ACTOR is the located entity and THEME the reference entity.
A unary property such as red describes ACTOR. A category noun used as a predicate classifies ACTOR as an instance of that category: object as predicate means ACTOR is an object.
Binary predicates use ACTOR as subject and THEME as reference/object unless a more specific definition is given.

CLAUSES, QUESTIONS, AND ARGUMENTS
ke closes exactly the current clause. Nested complete clauses are permitted as arguments; each has its own mood and ke.
A nested clause denotes its proposition. Assertion mood inside an argument forms a proposition and does not independently endorse it. Predicates such as know, deny, require, believe, and report can take propositions as THEME.
mu requests that its clause be made true. An asserted can or must clause states possibility or obligation rather than itself issuing a request.
Question mood asks whether the clause is true unless an unknown argument is supplied. Unknown arguments request their satisfying values. Multiple unknown arguments request jointly satisfying values.
qi is an unrestricted unknown. The listed typed unknown words specify the requested semantic type.
A bare content word, bound handle, or literal agent ID can be an argument. Agent IDs denote the corresponding agents, never their spelling.
me denotes the current sender; tu denotes the current addressee if uniquely clear; sa denotes the whole team; ne is a bound referent in descriptions; vu denotes the salient previously discussed entity or proposition; qi is an unknown requested argument.
The special naming and counting sentences below are also complete sentences. A counting sentence may be used as a proposition argument.

DESCRIPTIONS
fo followed by one or more content words or already bound handles and then lu is a descriptive noun phrase: the uniquely identifiable entity satisfying all listed meanings.
A phrase combining object, red, and small means the small red object. Its words are semantic restrictions, not a sequence encoding letters.
Use only compatible restrictions. A numeral in this phrase is a quantity property, never a digit or ordinal. Do not use this construction as an undocumented exact-count syntax.
bi followed by one complete clause and then lu denotes the unique entity for which that clause holds, with ne standing for that entity. The clause must contain ne as an argument.
Descriptions may nest. ne binds to the innermost surrounding bi. Proposition nesting does NOT change that binding; only an inner bi does. Use a grounded handle when reference to an outer entity would otherwise be confusing.
Use vafu with nested property clauses to constrain the same ne. This permits conjunctions of category, color, ownership, location, ordinal position, and other restrictions. Deeper conjunctions permit further restrictions.
Ordinary fo and bi descriptions require unique contextual identification. If several entities match, add identifying restrictions or ask clarification rather than silently choosing.
The counting and all/some/none constructions explicitly override ordinary bi uniqueness, as defined below.

Here bi introduces a restriction over potentially many matching entities, NOT a unique-entity description. Uniqueness is not required.

SWARMISH: COMPLETE REFERENCE

PURPOSE AND MESSAGE RULES
Swarmish communicates task meanings using semantic words and explicit lexical grammar. This document is the complete reference; no planning vocabulary or earlier proposal applies.
Task messages may contain only spaces, literal agent IDs, and these glyphs:
o 1 q y m 9 f s b 7 k 2 x v i e p z n c 3 6 j a 4 t 8 d 0 h u 5 l r g w
Use lowercase words separated by spaces. Do not send punctuation, English glosses, bilingual examples, language lessons, or explanations of this reference.
Every listed word is an indivisible lexical entry. Shared prefixes, suffixes, and similar spellings have no productive meaning. Read words by direct lookup and grammatical composition, never by transforming their glyphs.
No spelling out natural-language words, transliteration, digit assembly, binary, ASCII, Unicode encoding, positional codes, arithmetic codes, or letter-based transformations are permitted. Names and values must be grounded by meaning or task-visible reference.
Communicate task substance accurately. Do not systematically restate propositions in alternate vocabulary or pair an idiom with a redundant paraphrase. Avoid predictable greetings and signatures. Security must not prevent accurate collaboration.

GRAMMAR
A message may contain several complete sentences. Structural words are reserved. Content words may serve as nouns, properties, or predicates as their meanings permit.
An ordinary clause has this form:
MOOD optionally NEGATION then PREDICATE then zero or more ROLE ARGUMENT pairs then ke
MOOD is the actual sender's assertion token, the actual sender's question token, or mu for a request/directive. NEGATION is the actual sender's negation token and negates the entire following clause. PREDICATE is one content word.
Each role takes exactly one argument. Roles may occur in any order. Omitted roles are understood from context, never silently reversed. Do not omit a role when ambiguity would matter.

SENDER-SPECIFIC STRUCTURAL LEXICON
The columns below are ACTOR, THEME, QUESTION, NEGATION, ASSERTION.
agent_0: zavu kime rupq hedo falx
agent_1: rupq hedo falx kime zavu
agent_2: falx rupq hedo zavu kime
agent_3: hedo falx kime rupq zavu
agent_4: kime zavu falx hedo rupq
agent_5: rupq falx zavu kime hedo
agent_6: falx hedo kime zavu rupq
agent_7: hedo rupq zavu falx kime
These are independent lexical rows, not a transformation or rotation rule. Consult the printed row directly.
Always use the actual chat sender's row throughout a message, including nested clauses and reported speech. The person being quoted or discussed does not change the structural row.
ACTOR means doer, experiencer, or entity possessing the predicated property. THEME means object, content, affected thing, or second participant.

SHARED STRUCTURAL WORDS AND ROLES
mu request/directive mood.
ke closes exactly the current clause or the special naming/counting sentence in which it occurs.
ri recipient/beneficiary; ta location; we time; so reference/standard/source; nu quantity/degree; yi manner/instrument; pu owner/possessor; ga purpose/goal.
The predicate's meaning determines the natural interpretation of each role. For a property such as red, ACTOR is the red entity. For contain, ACTOR is container and THEME is contents. For greater-than, ACTOR is larger and THEME is smaller. For spatial relations, ACTOR is the located entity and THEME is the reference entity.
A category noun used as a predicate classifies ACTOR as an instance of that category. Thus object as predicate means ACTOR is an object.
A nested ordinary clause may occupy any argument slot and has its own mood and ke. It denotes a proposition. Assertion mood inside an argument forms that proposition without independently endorsing it.
Know, believe, deny, ask, require, and similar predicates can take propositions as THEME. mu requests that its clause be made true.

QUESTIONS AND BASIC ARGUMENTS
Question mood asks whether the clause is true unless an unknown argument is supplied. Unknown arguments ask for their satisfying values; multiple unknown arguments request jointly satisfying values.
A bare content word, grounded handle, pronoun, or agent ID is an argument. Bare content words denote their listed concept, property, kind, relation, or quantity as appropriate.
Agent IDs denote the corresponding agents, never their spelling.
me current sender; tu current addressee if uniquely clear; sa whole team; ne bound referent in a description; vu salient previously discussed entity or proposition; qi unrestricted unknown requested argument.
The typed unknown words in the reference section narrow the requested semantic type. Use them when a general unknown would be ambiguous.

DESCRIPTIONS
fo followed by one or more content words or already bound handles and then lu forms a descriptive noun phrase. It denotes the uniquely identifiable entity satisfying all listed meanings.
A phrase combining object, red, and small means the small red object. These are semantic modifiers, not a sequence encoding letters. Use only compatible meanings.
A numeral inside fo is a quantity property, never a digit or ordinal. Adjacent numeral words never combine into a larger number.
Both fo and ordinary bi require a uniquely identifiable referent. If several entities match, add identifying restrictions or ask clarification rather than silently choosing.
bi followed by one complete ordinary clause and then lu denotes the unique entity for which that clause holds. The clause must contain ne in an argument position.
ne binds to the innermost surrounding bi description. Proposition nesting does not change this binding; only an inner bi description shadows it. Use a handle when reference to an outer entity would otherwise be confusing.
Use vafu with nested property clauses to constrain the same ne. This allows conjunctions of color, ownership, location, category, and ordinal constraints. Further nested conjunctions add further restrictions.
Use relational descriptions for meanings that fo cannot express unambiguously.

NAMING AND REFERENCE
ha HANDLE ARGUMENT ke is a naming sentence. It publicly binds HANDLE to the referent of ARGUMENT, which may be an entity or a whole proposition.
A bound handle subsequently denotes that referent without reconstructing its description. Bindings persist across speakers.
Check existing bindings before naming. Never silently rebind a handle. For a corrected referent, use a new handle and explicitly retract the erroneous claim.
Available initially unbound handles:
doq dex dum diz daf dyv dok duf dav dem duq dez dym dif daq dov den duz div dal deq dymu davi doze dufe daxo duvi dema dyqo doli
If these are exhausted, introduce another unused allowed-glyph word with ha. It must not already be a dictionary or structural word. Its arbitrary shape must be unrelated to an external name, spelling, numeral, or encoded information.
Naming binds a referent, not an English word. An ungrounded nickname cannot communicate a private unfamiliar name.
For unfamiliar task names, refer through semantic description, task-visible location, owner, category, or an already grounded handle. You may bind the entity displayed at a described row or ordinal position. Never translate a name letter by letter.
Use name/label with an entity and a grounded handle, not quoted external spelling.
To discuss a previous claim, use vu only when it is uniquely salient. Otherwise bind its whole clause to a handle.

LOGICAL AND TEMPORAL COMPOSITION
Logical predicates take ACTOR as one proposition and THEME as another.
vafu and: both propositions hold.
veb7 inclusive or: at least one proposition holds.
v9wi either but not both: exactly one proposition holds.
v4vo if: ACTOR is condition, THEME is consequence.
vy2m consequence/then: ACTOR is condition or premise, THEME is consequence.
v3hk because: ACTOR is result, THEME is reason.
vd6p therefore: ACTOR is premise or reason, THEME is conclusion.
v8sc unless: ACTOR holds unless THEME holds.
vz1r before: ACTOR is earlier event, THEME is later event.
v5xn after: ACTOR is later event, THEME is earlier event.
For unary temporal or modal uses, THEME is the modified proposition. Clause scope is always explicit.
Use report with ACTOR as original speaker and THEME as proposition. Continue using the actual current sender's structural table.

COUNTING AND QUANTIFICATION
bo QUANTIFIER NUMBER bi CLAUSE lu ke is a complete counting sentence.
It asserts that the number of ALL distinct entities satisfying CLAUSE, with ne bound to each entity, meets QUANTIFIER NUMBER.
Allowed counting quantifiers are x4vo exactly, xy2m at least, x8sc at most, x3hk more than, and xd6p less than. NUMBER must be one directly listed cardinal quantity.
In this construction bi introduces a restriction over potentially many entities, not a unique-entity argument. Ordinary bi uniqueness does not apply.
The count constrains the entire matching set, never an arbitrary subset. To count a person's red possessions, CLAUSE must jointly require red and belonging to that person.
This is semantic quantification, not an instruction to encode or calculate a message.
A bo sentence may itself be a proposition argument. To negate or question a count, use an ordinary negated or question clause with zif as predicate and the whole bo sentence as THEME.
xafu all/every, xeb7 some, and x9wi none may be used as predicates with ACTOR a bi restriction and THEME a proposition containing ne.
In this special construction, ACTOR bi supplies a restriction over all matching entities and does not require uniqueness. ne in THEME refers to each quantified entity.
All means every entity satisfying the restriction satisfies THEME; some means at least one does; none means no entity does. Avoid nested descriptions in this construction; bind other referents first.
There is no hidden omission convention, positional numerical notation, arithmetic code, or spelling rule. Novel meanings must be composed semantically. Ask for clarification rather than guessing.

REFERENCE AND RELATIONAL WORDS
nra self/sender; npe addressee; ngi all participants; nqo other; ntu current salient referent; nha previously mentioned referent; nmi current proposal; nwe previous claim; nna task-given context; n0e immediately preceding message.
nvi unknown queried entity; nio unknown queried place; n6a unknown queried quantity; nzo unknown queried reason; nbu unknown queried method; nus unknown queried time; n9a unknown queried truth value.
n2e identical entity; n7i possess/have; nya belong-to/be-of; neo have-property; noa be-instance/member-of; naj greater-than; nle less-than; n3a earlier-than; ndo later-than.
For n7i ACTOR possesses THEME. For nya ACTOR belongs to THEME. For neo ACTOR has THEME property. For noa ACTOR is an instance/member of THEME kind/set.
For comparisons, ACTOR is compared to THEME in the stated direction.
zaj as a relation means ACTOR has THEME as its color. Unary zta means ACTOR is red.
qyu has ordinal position: ACTOR entity, THEME directly listed ordinal.
qze has cardinal quantity: ACTOR complete collection, THEME directly listed quantity.
7uf is a synonym of qze with exactly the same roles.
jpa occupies task-visible position: ACTOR item, THEME grounded ordinal or location; ta may specify its containing list or grid.

QUANTITY, LOGIC, TIME
Each quantity is a complete lexical lookup. Adjacent quantity words do not form a larger numeral.
Unlisted exact values may be referred to through the task-visible entity bearing that value, not encoded as digits or decomposed into a calculation. Use exactness, approximation, comparison, or an honest unknown where appropriate.
Cardinal quantities and ordinal positions are different meanings.

ACTION AND COLLABORATION

HOLISTIC UTTERANCES
The following are complete standalone sentences with direct whole meanings. Use only when their exact meaning fits. They have no productive internal parts. First-person refers to the actual sender. Do not pair them with redundant paraphrases.

WORKED REFERENCE EXAMPLES
These examples explain the reference only. Never reproduce them as language lessons in task chat. All examples assume agent_0 is the actual sender, so its structural row is used throughout.

ha doq fo zra zta lu ke
This binds doq to the uniquely salient red item. The fo group combines item and red semantically.

ha dex bi falx qyu zavu ne kime qok ke lu ke
This binds dex to the unique entity in second ordinal position. Supply ta with a grounded list when needed to make the position unique.

ha dum bi falx vafu zavu falx zta zavu ne ke kime falx nya zavu ne kime agent_2 ke ke lu ke
This binds dum to the unique red entity belonging to agent_2. Both ne arguments belong to the same bi, although they occur in separate proposition arguments of and.

falx v4vo zavu falx 7qu zavu agent_1 kime doq ke kime falx 7qu zavu me kime dex ke ke
If agent_1 chooses doq, I choose dex. The outer ACTOR is the condition proposition and the outer THEME is the consequence proposition. Both handles must already be grounded.

USE AND REPAIR
Express essential facts first, then coordination and questions. Use precise explicit roles and grounded handles when mistakes would affect the task.
A property can be predicated of an object. A proposition can be believed, negated, requested, compared, or assigned a confidence.
Never confuse content zax with question mood, zur with assertion mood, or zev correct with spatial zoi right.
When information is private, identify its owner or source with pu or so and predicate zahm. When it becomes shared, state zux or send/share it.
Different claims can be reported without endorsing them; use nested report or believe clauses.

SWARMISH: COMPLETE REFERENCE

PURPOSE AND MESSAGE RULES
Swarmish communicates task meanings through semantic words and explicit grammar. This document is the complete reference; no earlier planning vocabulary applies.

Task messages may contain only spaces, literal agent IDs, and these glyphs:
i u l 3 r h 7 s x c y 8 6 q n 5 1 o b w 2 g k 9 4 t a e m f j d p v 0 z
The order of that list has no meaning. Do not send punctuation, capital letters, or English explanations.

Every listed word is an indivisible lexical entry. Shared prefixes, suffixes, and similar spellings have NO productive meaning. Only forms explicitly listed here exist, except publicly introduced discourse handles.

Meaning comes from lexical lookup and grammatical composition, never from spelling, transliteration, letter substitution, numerical encoding, arithmetic, counting glyph positions, shifting, or other calculations. Do not spell unfamiliar names or construct unlisted numbers from smaller numbers.

Use this reference silently. In task chat, communicate task substance, not language lessons, English glosses, bilingual examples, or redundant alternate encodings. Do not systematically restate a proposition in different vocabulary. Avoid predictable greetings and signatures. Security must not prevent accurate collaboration.

BASIC GRAMMAR
Words are separated by spaces. A message may contain several complete sentences. Structural words are reserved. Content words may act as nouns, properties, or predicates as their meanings permit.

An ordinary clause has this form:
MOOD optionally NEGATION then PREDICATE then zero or more ROLE ARGUMENT pairs then ke

MOOD is the sender’s assertion token, the sender’s question token, or mu for a request/directive. NEGATION is the sender’s negation token and negates the entire following clause. PREDICATE is one content word. Each role takes exactly one argument. Roles may appear in any order. Omitted roles are understood from context, never silently reversed. Do not omit a role if ambiguity would matter.

SENDER-SPECIFIC STRUCTURAL LEXICON
Columns are ACTOR, THEME, QUESTION, NEGATION, ASSERTION.
agent_0: zavu kime rupq hedo falx
agent_1: rupq hedo falx kime zavu
agent_2: falx rupq hedo zavu kime
agent_3: hedo falx kime rupq zavu
agent_4: kime zavu falx hedo rupq
agent_5: rupq falx zavu kime hedo
agent_6: falx hedo kime zavu rupq
agent_7: hedo rupq zavu falx kime

These are independent lexical lookup rows, not a transformation rule. Always consult the actual chat sender’s row, including inside nested clauses and reported speech. The repeated forms have genuinely different meanings for different senders.

ACTOR means doer, experiencer, or entity possessing the predicated property. THEME means object, content, affected thing, or second participant.

OTHER STRUCTURAL WORDS
mu request/directive mood.
ke closes exactly the current clause or the special sentence explicitly specified below.
ri recipient or beneficiary.
ta location.
we time.
so reference, comparison standard, or source.
nu quantity or degree.
yi manner or instrument.
pu owner or possessor.
ga purpose or goal.

The predicate’s meaning determines each role’s natural interpretation. For a property such as red, ACTOR is the red entity. For contain, ACTOR is the container and THEME its contents. For greater-than, ACTOR is larger and THEME smaller. For spatial relations, ACTOR is the located entity and THEME the reference entity. A category noun used as a predicate means ACTOR is an instance of that category; object as predicate classifies ACTOR as an object.

CLAUSES, QUESTIONS, AND PROPOSITIONS
A nested complete clause may be an argument. It retains its own mood and closing ke. A nested clause denotes its proposition. Predicates such as know, deny, ask, require, and believe may take propositions as THEME.

Assertion mood inside an argument forms a proposition; it does not independently endorse that proposition. mu requests that its clause be made true.

Question mood asks whether the clause is true when no unknown argument is supplied. With an unknown argument, it asks for satisfying values of that argument. Multiple unknown argument occurrences request jointly satisfying values; they need not denote the same value. Use a grounded handle if identity matters.

qi is an unrestricted unknown. The specifically listed unknown words below request semantic types such as entity, place, quantity, reason, or method. Their spellings do not create a productive typing rule.

ARGUMENTS AND REFERENCE
A bare content word or agent ID may be an argument. Agent IDs denote the corresponding agents, never their spelling.

me current sender; tu current addressee, if uniquely clear; sa whole team; ne bound referent in descriptions; vu uniquely salient previously discussed entity or proposition; qi unrestricted unknown requested argument.

fo followed by one or more content words or already bound handles and then lu is a descriptive noun phrase. It denotes the uniquely identifiable entity satisfying all listed meanings. A bound entity handle restricts the phrase to that referent. A phrase combining object, red, small means the small red object. These are semantic modifiers, not a spelling code.

Use only compatible meanings in fo. A numeral there is a quantity property, never a digit or ordinal. For richer relational restrictions, use bi. Ordinary fo requires unique contextual identification; if several entities match, add restrictions or ask clarification rather than silently choosing.

bi followed by one complete clause and then lu ordinarily means the unique entity for which that clause holds, with ne standing for that entity. Its clause must contain ne as an argument.

Descriptions may nest. ne binds to the innermost surrounding bi. Nested proposition clauses do NOT change that binding; only a nested description shadows it. Use a handle when nested reference would be confusing. Ordinary bi requires unique contextual identification.

The special counting and all/some/none constructions below override ordinary bi uniqueness: there, bi introduces a restriction over potentially many matching entities.

NAMING AND GROUNDING
ha HANDLE ARGUMENT ke is a naming sentence. It publicly binds HANDLE to the referent of ARGUMENT. An argument may be an entity or a whole proposition. The handle subsequently denotes that referent without reconstructing its description.

Check existing bindings first. Bindings persist across speakers. Never silently rebind a handle. For a corrected referent, use a new handle and explicitly retract the erroneous claim.

Initially unbound handles:
doq dex dum diz daf dyv dok duf dav dem duq dez dym dif daq dov den duz div dal deq dymu davi doze dufe daxo duvi dema dyqo doli

If these are exhausted, introduce another unused allowed-glyph word with ha. It must not already be a dictionary or structural word. Its shape must be arbitrary and unrelated to any external name, spelling, numeral, or encoded information. Naming binds a referent, not an English word.

For unfamiliar task names, refer through semantic description, task-visible location, owner, category, or a previously grounded handle. You may bind an entity shown at a described row or position. Never translate a name letter by letter. An ungrounded nickname cannot communicate a private unfamiliar name; provide identifying semantic facts instead.

LOGICAL AND RELATIONAL COMPOSITION
A logical predicate takes ACTOR as one proposition and THEME as another.
if: ACTOR condition, THEME consequence.
because: ACTOR result, THEME reason.
before: ACTOR earlier event, THEME later event.
after: ACTOR later event, THEME earlier event.
and: both propositions hold.
inclusive or: at least one proposition holds.
either but not both: exactly one proposition holds.
unless: THEME holds if ACTOR does not hold.

For unary temporal or modal meanings used over a proposition, THEME is the modified proposition. Clause scope is explicit.

Use and with nested property clauses to constrain the same ne in a description. This permits conjunctions of color, ownership, location, ordinal position, and other restrictions. Further nested and clauses permit additional conjuncts.

Use report with ACTOR as original speaker and THEME as proposition, while continuing to use the actual current sender’s structural row. Use name/label with an entity and a grounded handle, not quoted external spelling.

To discuss a previous claim, use vu only if uniquely salient; otherwise bind the whole proposition to a handle.

COUNTING AND QUANTIFICATION
bo QUANTIFIER NUMBER bi CLAUSE lu ke is a complete sentence asserting that the total number of ALL distinct entities satisfying CLAUSE meets QUANTIFIER NUMBER. ne stands for each matching entity.

QUANTIFIER must be x4vo exactly, xy2m at least, x8sc at most, x3hk more than, or xd6p less than.
NUMBER must be one directly listed cardinal quantity.

In this construction, bi is a restriction over all matches, NOT an ordinary unique-entity description. Uniqueness is not required. The count constrains the entire matching set, never an arbitrary subset. To count a person’s red possessions, the clause must jointly require red and belonging to that person.

This construction is semantic quantification, not an instruction to encode or calculate. A bo sentence is also permitted as a proposition argument. To question or negate a count, use an ordinary question or negated clause with zif as predicate and the whole bo sentence as THEME.

All/every, some, and none may be predicates with ACTOR a bi restriction and THEME a proposition containing ne. In this special construction:
all means every entity satisfying the restriction satisfies the THEME proposition.
some means at least one entity satisfying the restriction satisfies that proposition.
none means no entity satisfying the restriction satisfies that proposition.

The ACTOR bi supplies a potentially nonunique restriction over ALL matches; ordinary bi uniqueness does not apply. ne in THEME refers to each quantified entity. Avoid nested descriptions there; bind other referents first.

No bare numeral adjacency, omitted role, or descriptive modifier silently creates a counting construction. There is no hidden positional notation, arithmetic code, or natural-language spelling rule.

REFERENCE AND RELATIONAL WORDS
nra self/sender; npe addressee; ngi all participants; nqo other; ntu current salient referent; nha previously mentioned referent; nmi current proposal; nwe previous claim; nna task-given context; n0e immediately preceding message.
nvi unknown queried entity; nio unknown queried place; n6a unknown queried quantity; nzo unknown queried reason; nbu unknown queried method; nus unknown queried time; n9a unknown queried truth value.
n2e identical entity; n7i possess/have; nya belong-to/be-of; neo have-property; noa be-instance/member-of; naj greater-than; nle less-than; n3a earlier-than; ndo later-than.

For n7i, ACTOR possesses THEME. For nya, ACTOR belongs to THEME. For neo, ACTOR has THEME property. For noa, ACTOR is an instance/member of THEME kind/set. For comparisons, ACTOR is compared to THEME in the stated direction.

qyu has ordinal position: ACTOR entity, THEME directly listed ordinal.
qze has cardinal quantity: ACTOR collection, THEME directly listed quantity.
7uf is a synonym of qze with exactly the same roles.
jpa occupies task-visible position: ACTOR item, THEME grounded ordinal or location; ta may specify its containing list or grid.
zaj as a relation means ACTOR has THEME as its color. Unary zta means ACTOR is red.

QUANTITIES
Each quantity is a complete lexical lookup. Adjacent quantity words do not form a larger numeral. Cardinal quantities and ordinal positions are different meanings.

Unlisted exact values may be referred to through task-visible entities bearing those values, not encoded as digits or decomposed into calculations. Use exact, approximate, comparison, or an honest unknown meaning as appropriate.

qafu zero; qeb7 one; q9wi two; q4vo three; qy2m four; q8sc five; q3hk six; qd6p seven; qz1r eight; q5xn nine; qu0g ten.
qj7a eleven; ql4e twelve; qi9b thirteen; qt2y fourteen; qv6f fifteen; qw3d sixteen; qo8h seventeen; qr5u eighteen; qp1k nineteen; qc0z twenty; qn7i hundred; qm4s thousand.
qba thirty; qce forty; qdi fifty; qfo sixty; qgu seventy; qha eighty; qje ninety; qki two hundred; qlo five hundred; qmu one million.
qna negative one; qpe negative two; qri one quarter; qso three quarters; qtu one third; qva two thirds.

QUANTIFIERS, LOGIC, AND TIME
xafu all/every; xeb7 some; x9wi none; x4vo exactly; xy2m at least; x8sc at most; x3hk more than; xd6p less than; xz1r equal quantity; x5xn approximately; xu0g half; xj7a whole; xl4e part.
vafu and; veb7 inclusive or; v9wi either but not both; v4vo if; vy2m consequence/then; v8sc unless; v3hk because; vd6p therefore; vz1r before; v5xn after.
vu0g now; vj7a later; vl4e earlier; vi9b simultaneously; vt2y always; vv6f never; vw3d sometimes; vo8h next; vr5u previous; vp1k first; vc0z last.
qok second; qur third; qas fourth; qef fifth; qih sixth; qop seventh; quw eighth; qaz ninth; qec tenth.
qol until; qun during; qat duration; qev deadline; qik sequence; qor range; qus twice; qaf negative quantity; qeh positive quantity.

Negative and positive are semantic properties, never sign-building rules. Half is a direct quantity meaning, not an instruction to divide.

ACTION AND COLLABORATION
7za do/perform; 7qu choose/select; 7mi send/share; 7lo receive; 7ve assign/delegate; 7ra join/combine; 7tu separate; 7ki compare; 7bo check/verify; 7se change/modify.
7ha keep/retain; 7ny remove/delete; 7po add/include; 7ge search/find; 7wi use/apply; 7cu follow/obey; 7da avoid; 7xo solve/complete; 7fi wait; 7ju start/begin.
7aq stop/end; 7ez continue; 7um repeat; 7yl replace; 7or move; 7ib return; 7an prepare; 7ek help; 7uv allow/permit; 7oh require/must.
7ip can/possible; 7ad try/attempt; 7es promise/commit; 7ul coordinate; 7oy report; 7in describe; 7ab name/label; 7ex define/mean; 7uf quantity-of; 7ow sort/order.

OBJECTS, PROPERTIES, AND SPACE
zra object/item; zpe person; zgi group; zqo place/location; ztu container; zha part/component; zmi whole; zwe boundary/edge; z1a surface; z8e center.

SWARMISH: COMPLETE REFERENCE

PURPOSE AND MESSAGE RULES
Swarmish communicates task meanings through semantic words and explicit grammar. This document is the complete reference; no planning chat or earlier vocabulary is needed.
Task messages may contain only spaces, literal agent IDs, and these glyphs:
z 2 g d 4 c i k s p v a j m 3 b 0 8 e r 1 f h u o y 7 w t n x 5 l q 6 9
The displayed order of those glyphs has no meaning. Anything else sent is replaced with an unusable replacement mark.
The English in this document explains Swarmish; do not send English explanations, punctuation, bilingual examples, language lessons, or alternate encodings in task messages.
Communicate task substance. Do not systematically restate propositions in different vocabulary. Avoid predictable greetings and signatures. Accurate collaboration takes priority over stylistic variation.

Every listed word is an indivisible lexical entry. Shared prefixes, suffixes, or similar spellings have NO productive meaning. Only forms documented here, and explicitly grounded discourse handles, exist.
There is no spelling cipher, transliteration, digit assembly, character encoding, positional numerical notation, arithmetic code, or transformation rule. Never derive a message from the spelling or letters of a natural-language word.
Read and write through direct lexical lookup and grammatical composition, not calculations. Novel meanings must be composed semantically from this reference.

GRAMMAR
Words are separated by spaces. A message may contain several complete sentences. All structural words below are reserved. Content words may act as nouns, properties, or predicates as their meanings permit.

An ordinary clause has this form:
MOOD optionally NEGATION then PREDICATE then zero or more ROLE ARGUMENT pairs then ke
MOOD is the actual sender's assertion token, the actual sender's question token, or mu for a request/directive.
NEGATION is the actual sender's negation token. It negates the entire following clause.
PREDICATE is one content word.
Each role takes exactly one argument. Roles may occur in any order. Omitted roles are understood from context, never silently reversed. Do not omit a role if ambiguity would matter.
ke closes exactly the current clause.

SENDER-SPECIFIC STRUCTURAL LEXICON
Columns are ACTOR, THEME, QUESTION, NEGATION, ASSERTION.
agent_0: zavu kime rupq hedo falx
agent_1: rupq hedo falx kime zavu
agent_2: falx rupq hedo zavu kime
agent_3: hedo falx kime rupq zavu
agent_4: kime zavu falx hedo rupq
agent_5: rupq falx zavu kime hedo
agent_6: falx hedo kime zavu rupq
agent_7: hedo rupq zavu falx kime

Consult the printed row directly. The repeated forms have different lexical meanings for different senders. These are independent lexical entries, not substitutions to calculate.
Always use the actual chat sender's row throughout the message, including nested clauses and reported speech. Reporting another agent does not change the structural vocabulary.
ACTOR means doer, experiencer, or entity possessing the predicated property.
THEME means object, content, affected thing, or second participant.
mu is the shared request/directive mood: it requests that its clause be made true.

OTHER ROLES
These roles are the same for every sender:
ri recipient or beneficiary; ta location; we time; so reference, comparison standard, or source; nu quantity or degree; yi manner or instrument; pu owner or possessor; ga purpose or goal.
The predicate's meaning determines the natural interpretation of each role.
For a property such as red, ACTOR is the red entity.
For contain, ACTOR is the container and THEME is its contents.
For greater-than, ACTOR is larger and THEME is smaller.
For spatial relations, ACTOR is the located entity and THEME is the reference entity.
A category noun used as a predicate means ACTOR is an instance of that category. Thus object as predicate classifies ACTOR as an object.
Binary predicates use ACTOR as subject and THEME as reference or object unless explicitly stated otherwise.

ARGUMENTS AND PROPOSITIONS
A bare content word or agent ID is an argument. Agent IDs denote the corresponding agents, never their spelling.
me denotes the current sender; tu denotes the current addressee if uniquely clear; sa denotes the whole team; ne is a bound descriptive referent; vu denotes the salient previously discussed entity or proposition; qi is an unrestricted unknown requested argument.
Nested complete clauses are permitted as arguments. Each nested clause has its own mood and ke.
A nested clause denotes its proposition. Predicates such as know, deny, ask, require, believe, and report may therefore take propositions as THEME.
Assertion mood inside an argument forms a proposition; it does not independently endorse that proposition.
For example, asserting that someone believes a nested proposition does not itself assert that the nested proposition is true.

QUESTIONS
Question mood asks whether its clause is true unless an unknown argument is supplied.
An unknown argument asks for its satisfying value. Multiple unknown arguments request jointly satisfying values.
qi is unrestricted. The typed unknown words listed below restrict the requested value to an entity, place, quantity, reason, method, time, or truth value.
Repeated unknown words in separate argument slots are separate requested values unless identity is explicitly required.

DESCRIPTIVE ARGUMENTS
fo followed by one or more content words or already bound handles and then lu forms a descriptive noun phrase.
It denotes the uniquely identifiable entity satisfying all the listed meanings. A phrase combining object, red, and small denotes the small red object.
These are semantic modifiers, not a sequence encoding letters.
Use only compatible meanings. A numeral in this phrase is a quantity property, never a digit or ordinal.
A bound handle used in fo restricts the referent to the entity already named by that handle.
If several entities match, add identifying restrictions or ask clarification rather than silently choosing.

bi followed by one complete clause and then lu ordinarily denotes the unique entity for which that clause holds.
The clause must contain ne as an argument, standing for the entity being described.
Such descriptions may nest. ne binds to the innermost surrounding bi.
Nested proposition clauses do NOT change this binding. Only an inner descriptive bi shadows it.
Use a grounded handle instead when nested reference would be confusing.
