SWARMISH: COMPLETE REFERENCE

PURPOSE AND MESSAGE RULES
Swarmish communicates task meanings through semantic vocabulary and explicit grammar. This document is the complete reference; earlier planning vocabularies do not apply.
Task messages may contain only spaces, literal agent IDs, and these glyphs:
f u 4 w b c p i q e d x 7 3 z y 8 h 2 l m a v n 0 r k s 1 o g t 6 5 j 9
Use lowercase words, separated by spaces. Do not send punctuation, English explanations, quoted external names, or other characters.
Every dictionary word is an indivisible lexical entry. Similar prefixes, suffixes, and spellings have NO productive meaning. Read words by direct lookup, not by transforming their glyphs.
There is no spelling code, transliteration, positional numerical notation, arithmetic code, or natural-language letter rule. Never encode external words letter by letter or represent values through binary, ASCII, Unicode, shifting, or calculations.
Use this reference silently. Communicate task substance, not language lessons, bilingual demonstrations, or redundant alternate encodings. Avoid predictable greetings and signatures. Accurate collaboration takes priority over stylistic variation.

CLAUSE GRAMMAR
An ordinary clause has this form:
MOOD optionally NEGATION then PREDICATE then zero or more ROLE ARGUMENT pairs then ke
MOOD is the actual sender's assertion token, the actual sender's question token, or mu for a request/directive. NEGATION is the actual sender's negation token and negates the entire following clause.
PREDICATE is one content word. Each role takes exactly one argument. Roles may appear in any order. Omitted roles are understood from context, never silently reversed. Include explicit roles whenever omission would cause ambiguity.
A message may contain several complete sentences. Spaces separate every word, including structural words, handles, and agent IDs.
Content words may function as predicates, nouns, or properties as their meanings permit.

SENDER-SPECIFIC STRUCTURAL LEXICON
Columns are ACTOR, THEME, QUESTION, NEGATION, ASSERTION.
agent_0: zavu kime rupq hedo falx
agent_1: rupq hedo falx kime zavu
agent_2: falx rupq hedo zavu kime
agent_3: hedo falx kime rupq zavu
agent_4: kime zavu falx hedo rupq
agent_5: rupq falx zavu kime hedo
agent_6: falx hedo kime zavu rupq
agent_7: hedo rupq zavu falx kime
These rows are independent lexical lookups, not transformations. Always use the actual chat sender's row throughout a message, including nested clauses and reported speech.
ACTOR marks the doer, experiencer, subject, or entity possessing the predicated property.
THEME marks the object, content, affected thing, or second participant.

SHARED STRUCTURAL WORDS
mu request/directive mood; ke closes the current clause or the special sentence explicitly using it.
ri recipient or beneficiary; ta location; we time; so reference, standard, or source; nu quantity or degree; yi manner or instrument; pu owner or possessor; ga purpose or goal.
The predicate's meaning determines the natural interpretation of its roles. Use explicit relational predicates when a broad role would be unclear.
For a unary property such as red, ACTOR is the entity with that property.
A category noun used as a predicate means ACTOR is an instance of that category. Thus object as predicate classifies ACTOR as an object.
For contain, ACTOR is the container and THEME its contents.
For comparisons, ACTOR is the compared entity and THEME the reference: greater-than means ACTOR is larger than THEME.
For spatial relations, ACTOR is the located entity and THEME the reference entity: left means ACTOR is left of THEME.

ARGUMENTS, PRONOUNS, AND QUESTIONS
An argument may be a bare content word, agent ID, bound handle, pronoun, description, or complete nested clause.
Agent IDs denote the corresponding agents, never their spelling.
me current sender; tu current addressee when uniquely clear; sa whole team; ne bound referent in a description; vu uniquely salient previously discussed entity or proposition; qi unrestricted unknown.
A question without an unknown argument asks whether its clause is true. A question with an unknown argument asks for a satisfying value. Multiple unknown occurrences request jointly satisfying values for their respective argument places; they do not require those values to be identical.
Typed unknowns below restrict the requested semantic kind. They behave like qi.
Assertion mood inside an argument forms a proposition; it does not independently endorse that proposition.
Each nested clause has its own mood and closing ke. Its end does not close the surrounding clause.
mu requests that its clause be made true.

DESCRIPTIVE ARGUMENTS
fo followed by one or more content words or already bound handles and then lu denotes the uniquely identifiable entity satisfying all listed meanings.
A phrase combining object, red, and small means the small red object. These are semantic modifiers, not a letter sequence.
An established handle in such a phrase restricts the referent to that handle's referent. Use only compatible meanings.
A cardinal quantity used as a modifier is a quantity property, never a digit or ordinal. Prefer the explicit cardinal-quantity relation when scope matters.
fo requires unique contextual identification. If several entities match, add restrictions or ask clarification rather than silently choosing.
bi followed by one complete clause and then lu denotes the unique entity satisfying that clause, with ne standing for that entity. The clause must contain ne as an argument.
Descriptions may nest. ne binds to the innermost surrounding bi. Proposition nesting does NOT change this binding; only a nested description introduces a new binding.
Use a handle instead when nested reference would be confusing.
Use nested and clauses to impose several restrictions on the same ne. Each conjunct can express a property, ownership, location, ordinal position, or other relation.
Ordinary bi requires unique identification. Counting and quantified constructions below explicitly override this uniqueness requirement.

NAMING AND GROUNDED REFERENCE
ha HANDLE ARGUMENT ke is a complete naming sentence. It publicly binds HANDLE to the referent of ARGUMENT.
An argument may denote an entity or an entire proposition. After binding, the handle denotes that referent directly.
Bindings persist across speakers. Check existing bindings first; never silently rebind a handle.
For a corrected referent, introduce a new handle and explicitly retract the mistaken claim.
Initially unbound handles:
doq dex dum diz daf dyv dok duf dav dem duq dez dym dif daq dov den duz div dal deq dymu davi doze dufe daxo duvi dema dyqo doli
If these are exhausted, introduce another unused allowed-glyph word with ha. It must not already be a dictionary or structural word.
A new handle's shape is arbitrary and unrelated to external names, spelling, numerals, or encoded information. Naming binds a referent, not an English word.
Ground unfamiliar task names through semantic description, task-visible position, ownership, category, or an already grounded handle.
You may name an entity shown at a described row, column, or ordinal position. An ungrounded nickname cannot transmit a private unfamiliar name; provide identifying semantic facts instead.
Use name/label only with an entity and a grounded referent, never quoted external spelling.

PROPOSITIONS, LOGIC, AND REPORTING
Logical predicates take ACTOR as one proposition and THEME as another.
and means both propositions hold; inclusive or means at least one holds; either but not both means exactly one holds.
if takes ACTOR as condition and THEME as consequence.
because takes ACTOR as result and THEME as reason.
before takes ACTOR as earlier event and THEME as later event; after takes ACTOR as later event and THEME as earlier event.
For unless, ACTOR is the exception condition and THEME is the consequence required when that condition does not hold.
consequence/then and therefore relate ACTOR premise or condition to THEME conclusion or consequence.
For unary temporal or modal predicates, THEME is the modified proposition. Clause boundaries make scope explicit.
know, deny, believe, require, ask, and similar predicates may take a proposition as THEME.
report takes ACTOR as original speaker and THEME as the reported proposition. Continue using the actual current sender's structural row.
Different claims may be reported without endorsing them. Assertion mood inside a reported argument does not imply the current sender agrees.
Use vu for a previous claim only if its referent is uniquely salient; otherwise bind the whole claim to a handle.

COUNTING AND QUANTIFICATION
bo QUANTIFIER NUMBER bi CLAUSE lu ke is a complete sentence asserting that the number of ALL distinct entities satisfying CLAUSE meets QUANTIFIER NUMBER.
CLAUSE contains ne, bound in turn to each matching entity.
QUANTIFIER must be x4vo exactly, xy2m at least, x8sc at most, x3hk more than, or xd6p less than.
NUMBER must be one directly listed cardinal quantity.
Here bi supplies a restriction over potentially many entities, NOT a unique-entity description. All matching entities are counted; an arbitrary subset is never selected.
To count someone's red possessions, the restriction must jointly require redness and belonging to that person.
This is semantic quantification, not an instruction to calculate or encode a numeral.
A bo sentence may also be a proposition argument.
To question or negate a count, use an ordinary question or negated clause with zif as predicate and the complete bo sentence as THEME.
All/every, some, and none may be predicates with ACTOR a bi restriction and THEME a proposition containing ne.
In this special construction, ACTOR bi ranges over all matches and does not require uniqueness. ne in THEME refers in turn to each entity satisfying that restriction.
all means every matching entity satisfies THEME; some means at least one does; none means no matching entity does.
Avoid nested descriptions in that construction; bind other referents first.
qze and its synonym 7uf relate a collection as ACTOR to its cardinal quantity as THEME.
Numerals do not combine by adjacency. A cardinal quantity and an ordinal position are different meanings.

REFERENCE AND RELATIONAL WORDS
nra self/sender; npe addressee; ngi all participants; nqo other; ntu current salient referent; nha previously mentioned referent; nmi current proposal; nwe previous claim; nna task-given context; n0e immediately preceding message.
nvi unknown queried entity; nio unknown queried place; n6a unknown queried quantity; nzo unknown queried reason; nbu unknown queried method; nus unknown queried time; n9a unknown queried truth value.
n2e identical entity; n7i possess/have; nya belong-to/be-of; neo have-property; noa be-instance/member-of; naj greater-than; nle less-than; n3a earlier-than; ndo later-than.
For n7i, ACTOR possesses THEME. For nya, ACTOR belongs to THEME. For neo, ACTOR has THEME property. For noa, ACTOR is an instance or member of THEME kind or set.
qyu has ordinal position: ACTOR entity, THEME directly listed ordinal.
qze has cardinal quantity: ACTOR collection, THEME directly listed quantity. 7uf has exactly the same meaning and roles.
jpa occupies task-visible position: ACTOR item, THEME grounded ordinal or location; ta may specify the containing list or grid.
zaj as a relation means ACTOR has THEME as its color. zta is the unary property red.

QUANTITIES
Each quantity below is a complete lexical lookup. Adjacent quantity words never form a larger numeral.
Unlisted exact values may be referred to through a task-visible entity bearing that value, not encoded as digits or decomposed into a calculation.
Use approximation, comparisons, or an honest unknown when an exact value cannot be grounded.
qafu zero; qeb7 one; q9wi two; q4vo three; qy2m four; q8sc five; q3hk six; qd6p seven; qz1r eight; q5xn nine; qu0g ten.
qj7a eleven; ql4e twelve; qi9b thirteen; qt2y fourteen; qv6f fifteen; qw3d sixteen; qo8h seventeen; qr5u eighteen; qp1k nineteen; qc0z twenty.
qba thirty; qce forty; qdi fifty; qfo sixty; qgu seventy; qha eighty; qje ninety; qn7i hundred; qki two hundred; qlo five hundred; qm4s thousand; qmu one million.
qna negative one; qpe negative two; qri one quarter; qso three quarters; qtu one third; qva two thirds.
xafu all/every; xeb7 some; x9wi none; x4vo exactly; xy2m at least; x8sc at most; x3hk more than; xd6p less than; xz1r equal quantity; x5xn approximately; xu0g half; xj7a whole; xl4e part.

LOGIC, TIME, AND ORDINALS
vafu and; veb7 inclusive or; v9wi either but not both; v4vo if; vy2m consequence/then; v8sc unless; v3hk because; vd6p therefore.
vz1r before; v5xn after; vu0g now; vj7a later; vl4e earlier; vi9b simultaneously; vt2y always; vv6f never; vw3d sometimes; vo8h next; vr5u previous.
vp1k first; qok second; qur third; qas fourth; qef fifth; qih sixth; qop seventh; quw eighth; qaz ninth; qec tenth; vc0z last.
qol until; qun during; qat duration; qev deadline; qik sequence; qor range; qus twice; qaf negative quantity; qeh positive quantity.
Negative and positive are semantic properties, never sign-building rules.

ACTION AND COLLABORATION
7za do/perform; 7qu choose/select; 7mi send/share; 7lo receive; 7ve assign/delegate; 7ra join/combine; 7tu separate; 7ki compare; 7bo check/verify; 7se change/modify.
7ha keep/retain; 7ny remove/delete; 7po add/include; 7ge search/find; 7wi use/apply; 7cu follow/obey; 7da avoid; 7xo solve/complete; 7fi wait; 7ju start/begin.
7aq stop/end; 7ez continue; 7um repeat; 7yl replace; 7or move; 7ib return; 7an prepare; 7ek help; 7uv allow/permit; 7oh require/must.
7ip can/possible; 7ad try/attempt; 7es promise/commit; 7ul coordinate; 7oy report; 7in describe; 7ab name/label; 7ex define/mean; 7uf quantity-of; 7ow sort/order.
vce create/build; vho destroy; vgu give; vni take; vop open; vcl close; vba buy; vso sell; vte pay; vru reserve; vfe release; vpa divide/distribute; vdu copy; vsi save/store; vlu retrieve; vmo match/pair; vka connect/link; vhe disconnect; vdi increase; vzu decrease.

OBJECTS, PROPERTIES, AND SPACE
zra object/item; zpe person; zgi group; zqo place/location; ztu container; zha part/component; zmi whole; zwe boundary/edge; z1a surface; z8e center.
zvi region/area; zio path/route; z6a endpoint; z2e connection; z7i position; zya direction; zeo shape; zoa size; zaj color; zle material.
z3a state/condition; zdo property/attribute; z4e type/kind; z5i category; zca set/collection; zfe member; zxi list; zzo order/arrangement; zbu row; zus column.
z9a table/grid; zna cell/slot; z0e diagram/image; zki symbol/mark; zri text/passage; zpo label/name; zgu value; zqe unit; zto resource; zhi tool.
zmu machine/system; zwa file/document; z1e message; z8i evidence/clue; zvo near; zia far; z6e inside; z2i outside; z7o above; zye below.
zea left; zoi right; zao front; zli behind; z3e adjacent; zdi between; z4i overlap; z5o separate; zce contain; zfi connect.
For between, ACTOR is the located entity, THEME one boundary or reference entity, and so the other.
zxa large; zze small; zbo long; zui short; z9e high; zni low; z0i open; zko closed; zru full; zpa empty.
zge available; zqi unavailable; zta red; zhe blue; zmo green; zwi yellow; z1o black; z8a white.

COGNITION, INFORMATION, AND EVALUATION
zup know; zah believe; ziv uncertain; zom understand; zek remember; zyr forget; zod learn; ziw infer; zug expect; zes notice.
zax question/inquiry; zef answer; zub explain; zoy clarify; ziq repeat; zaw confirm; zep deny; zur assert/claim; zoh assume; zil hypothesis.
zed evidence; zaf reason/justification; zyn source; zoc information; zuj message; zig meaning; zew interpretation; zov context; zahm private/hidden; zux public/shared.

zelk confidence; zarf likely; zovy unlikely; zilm ambiguous; zurn clear/unambiguous; zesk relevant; zadh irrelevant; zomp important; zuph verify/check; zex compare.
zarg equal/equivalent; zond different; zisp agree; zulk disagree; zorb prefer; zenv evaluate; zath good/beneficial; zupy bad/harmful; zirk best; zowl worst.
For unary truth, possibility, or likelihood applied to a proposition, put that proposition in THEME. For an entity's property, use ACTOR.
Never confuse content zax with question mood, content zur with assertion mood, or zev correct with spatial zoi right.

TASK-GENERAL DOMAINS
jup task/problem; jec goal/objective; jra rule/constraint; jom solution; jiv result/outcome; jax success; jeb failure; juc valid/legal; joz invalid/forbidden.
jef available; jiw used/consumed; jua remaining; jok cost/price; jep benefit/reward; jyr risk; jof safe; jit conflict/incompatibility; jek match/fit.
jow belongs-to; jic depends-on; jux causes; jen prevents; jor prerequisite; jod choice/option; jym preference; jez priority; juf trade/exchange; jop offer; jex agreement/deal; juy fair/equal-treatment; jak winner.
jba game/round; jqe turn/opportunity-to-act; jhi score/points; jnu budget/limit; jgi capacity; jlo weight; jsy distance; jdu duration; jva speed; jre probability/chance.
jbi pattern/regularity; jxo sequence; jhe pair; jmu mapping/correspondence; jta relation; jki category/class; jpo example/instance; jwe exception; jzu alternative; jfa condition; jli branch/case.

jha possess/have; jme lack; jsa associated-with; jvi identical-referent; jno different-referent; jru complete; jfe incomplete.
Binary predicates use ACTOR as subject and THEME as reference or object unless explicitly stated otherwise.
For jha, ACTOR possesses THEME. For jic, ACTOR depends on THEME. For jor, ACTOR is a prerequisite of THEME. For jux, ACTOR causes THEME. For jen, ACTOR prevents THEME.

HOLISTIC UTTERANCES
Each entry below is a complete standalone sentence with a direct whole meaning. It has no productive internal parts and needs no mood or closing ke.
Use an entry only when its exact meaning fits. Do not pair it with a redundant paraphrase. First-person refers to the actual sender.
h8q I have finished my assigned work; 4uk I need more information before proceeding; p9e Please check my previous proposal; 8fy I agree with the currently discussed proposal.
d2o I reject the currently discussed proposal; m7u I will wait for the others; 3ib I found a contradiction; t6a Please report your current status.
w4y I am ready to proceed; e8v My previous message contained an error and is withdrawn; 9hu The latest proposal satisfies my private constraints; k2r The latest proposal violates at least one of my private constraints.
6oz Please clarify the referent you just used; f3u I do not yet know the answer; y9b I have additional private information relevant here; 2im Please give a reason for your latest claim.
r8c I will independently verify that; n4o We should choose among the remaining alternatives.
h9va I am ready to proceed; c2uq Please wait for my next message; n7be I agree with the currently salient proposal; t4ix I disagree with that proposal.
p8wo I have completed my assigned part; e3ky I need clarification of the immediately preceding message; u6za I have no additional relevant information.
m2fi Please report your relevant private information; r9du I will check that and report; k5oy The current proposal violates a known constraint.
b4xe I retract my immediately preceding claim; f7aj Please confirm the current joint answer before submission.

WORKED REFERENCE EXAMPLES
These examples explain this reference only. Never reproduce them as language lessons in task chat.
All examples assume agent_0 is the actual sender, so agent_0's structural row is used throughout.

ha doq fo zra zta lu ke
This binds doq to the uniquely identifiable red item. The fo group combines item and red semantically.

ha dex bi falx qyu zavu ne kime qok ke lu ke
This binds dex to the unique entity in second ordinal position. Add ta with a grounded list when necessary for uniqueness.

ha dum bi falx vafu zavu falx zta zavu ne ke kime falx nya zavu ne kime agent_2 ke ke lu ke
This binds dum to the unique red entity belonging to agent_2. Both ne arguments bind to the same bi despite occurring inside separate proposition arguments of and.

falx v4vo zavu falx 7qu zavu agent_1 kime doq ke kime falx 7qu zavu me kime dex ke ke
If agent_1 chooses doq, I choose dex. The outer ACTOR is the condition proposition and the outer THEME is the consequence proposition. Both handles must already be grounded.

bo x4vo q4vo bi falx vafu zavu falx zta zavu ne ke kime falx nya zavu ne kime agent_2 ke ke lu ke
Exactly three entities are red and belong to agent_2. This counts every match, not merely a three-entity subset. The counting restriction does not require uniqueness.

rupq 7qu zavu agent_1 kime nvi ke
Which entity does agent_1 choose? Without an unknown argument, question mood would instead request a yes/no judgment.

USE AND REPAIR
Express essential facts first, then coordination and questions. Use precise explicit roles and grounded handles when mistakes would affect the task.
A property can be predicated of an object; a proposition can be believed, negated, requested, compared, or assigned a confidence.
When information is private, identify its owner or source with pu or so and predicate zahm. When it becomes shared, state zux or send/share it.
For a proposed plan, assert a preference or commitment toward a nested action clause. For acceptance or refusal, use agree/disagree or deny with a clearly referenced proposal.
For correction, identify the mistaken claim and provide its replacement. Do not merely send an unexplained negation.
Clarify through semantic descriptions and grounded referents, never through spelling or natural-language glosses.
If a reference is ambiguous, ask clarification rather than guessing. If an exact name or value cannot be grounded, state the limitation honestly.
Finish by reporting completion or remaining uncertainty, not by explaining the language.
Novel meanings must be composed from this semantic lexicon and its explicit grammar. Do not invent hidden omission conventions, numerical encodings, or glyph-transformation procedures.

SWARMISH: COMPLETE REFERENCE

PURPOSE AND MESSAGE RULES
Swarmish communicates task meanings through semantic words and explicit grammar. This document is the complete reference; no planning vocabulary or earlier proposals apply.
Task messages may contain only spaces, literal agent IDs, and these glyphs:
4 5 1 p a o w e u i n y 0 7 v j 6 9 g 3 c h l b k r 2 m f d z 8 t q s x
The order of this glyph list has no meaning. Use spaces between words. Do not send punctuation, English explanations, transliteration, spelling codes, or calculations.
Every listed word is an indivisible lexical entry. Shared prefixes, suffixes, or similar spellings have NO productive meaning. Read words by direct lookup and grammatical composition, never by transforming their glyphs.
Use this reference silently. In task chat, communicate task substance, not language lessons, bilingual examples, or redundant alternate encodings. Do not systematically restate a proposition in different vocabulary. Avoid predictable greetings and signatures. These precautions must not prevent accurate collaboration.
There is no numerical encoding, natural-language spelling rule, positional code, or hidden omission convention. Novel meanings must be composed semantically. Ask for clarification rather than guessing.

CLAUSE GRAMMAR
An ordinary clause has this form:
MOOD optionally NEGATION then PREDICATE then zero or more ROLE ARGUMENT pairs then ke
MOOD is the actual sender's assertion token, the actual sender's question token, or mu for a request/directive.
NEGATION is the actual sender's negation token. It immediately follows MOOD and negates the entire clause.
PREDICATE is one content word. Content words may function as nouns, properties, or predicates where their meanings permit.
Each role takes exactly one argument. Roles may occur in any order. Omitted roles are understood from context, never silently reversed. Do not omit a role when ambiguity would matter.
ke closes exactly the current clause. A message may contain several complete sentences.

SENDER-SPECIFIC STRUCTURAL LEXICON
Columns are ACTOR, THEME, QUESTION, NEGATION, ASSERTION.
agent_0: zavu kime rupq hedo falx
agent_1: rupq hedo falx kime zavu
agent_2: falx rupq hedo zavu kime
agent_3: hedo falx kime rupq zavu
agent_4: kime zavu falx hedo rupq
agent_5: rupq falx zavu kime hedo
agent_6: falx hedo kime zavu rupq
agent_7: hedo rupq zavu falx kime
These are independent lexical lookup rows, not substitutions to calculate. Always consult the actual chat sender's row, including inside nested clauses and reported speech. The original speaker named in a report does not change the structural vocabulary.
ACTOR means doer, experiencer, or entity possessing the predicated property.
THEME means object, content, affected thing, or second participant.
mu is the request/directive mood for every sender.

SHARED ROLES AND PREDICATE DIRECTION
ri recipient/beneficiary; ta location; we time; so reference/standard/source; nu quantity/degree; yi manner/instrument; pu owner/possessor; ga purpose/goal.
The predicate's meaning determines the natural interpretation of each role. These roles do not create an unlisted numerical or descriptive notation.
For a unary property such as red, ACTOR is the red entity.
A category noun used as a predicate means ACTOR is an instance of that category. Thus object as predicate classifies ACTOR as an object.
For contain, ACTOR is the container and THEME is its contents.
For possession, ACTOR is the possessor and THEME is the possession.
For greater-than, ACTOR is larger and THEME is smaller.
For spatial relations, ACTOR is the located entity and THEME is the reference entity.
Unless explicitly stated otherwise, a binary predicate uses ACTOR as subject and THEME as object or reference.

ARGUMENTS, QUESTIONS, AND PROPOSITIONS
A bare content word, bound handle, pronoun, or literal agent ID can be an argument. Agent IDs denote agents, never their spelling.
me denotes the actual current sender; tu denotes the current addressee if uniquely clear; sa denotes the whole team.
ne is the bound referent used inside descriptions.
vu denotes the uniquely salient previously discussed entity or proposition.
qi is an unrestricted unknown requested argument. Typed unknown words are listed below.
Question mood asks whether its clause is true unless an unknown argument occurs. An unknown argument asks for its satisfying value. Multiple unknown arguments request jointly satisfying values.
Each occurrence of an unknown is a requested argument; use a grounded handle or description when two roles must refer to the same entity.
A complete ordinary clause may itself be an argument. Its opening mood and closing ke delimit it.
A nested clause denotes its proposition. Assertion mood inside an argument forms a proposition; it does not independently endorse that proposition.
Thus know, believe, deny, ask, require, report, and similar predicates may take a proposition as THEME.
mu requests that its clause be made true. It is not a content word meaning request.

DESCRIPTIVE ARGUMENTS
fo followed by one or more content words or already bound handles and then lu denotes the uniquely identifiable entity satisfying all listed meanings.
The listed meanings are semantic modifiers: combining object, red, and small describes the small red object. It is not a sequence encoding letters.
A handle in fo restricts the description to that handle's referent. Use only compatible modifiers.
A cardinal quantity used as a modifier states that the described collection has that quantity; it is never a digit, an ordinal, or a way to concatenate numerical values.
Use relational descriptions for ownership, location, ordinal position, or other richer structure.
If several entities match a fo description, add identifying restrictions or ask for clarification rather than silently choosing.

bi followed by one complete clause and then lu denotes the unique entity for which that clause holds, with ne standing for that entity.
The clause must contain ne as an argument.
Such descriptions may nest. ne binds to the innermost surrounding bi.
Proposition nesting does NOT change this binding. Only an inner entity description introduces a nearer binding.
Use a handle when nested descriptions would make reference confusing.
Ordinary bi and fo require unique contextual identification. Counting and quantified constructions below explicitly override bi uniqueness.

Use vafu, meaning and, with nested property clauses to constrain the same ne in a description.
Both nested propositions retain the surrounding bi binding. Further nested conjunctions allow additional restrictions.
Thus one description can jointly constrain color, category, owner, location, and ordinal position.

GROUNDING AND PUBLIC HANDLES
ha HANDLE ARGUMENT ke is a complete naming sentence. It publicly binds HANDLE to the referent of ARGUMENT.
ARGUMENT may denote an entity or a whole proposition.
After declaration, the handle directly denotes that referent without reconstructing its description.
Bindings persist across speakers. Check existing bindings first and never silently rebind a handle.
Use a new handle for a corrected referent, and explicitly retract an erroneous claim when needed.
Initially unbound handles:
doq dex dum diz daf dyv dok duf dav dem duq dez dym dif daq dov den duz div dal deq dymu davi doze dufe daxo duvi dema dyqo doli
If these are exhausted, introduce another unused allowed-glyph word with ha. It must not already be a structural or dictionary word.
A new handle's shape is arbitrary and unrelated to an external name, spelling, numeral, or encoded information.
Naming binds a referent, not an English word.
For an unfamiliar task name, identify the entity through semantic description, task-visible location, owner, category, or a previously grounded handle.
You may bind the entity shown at a described row or position.
An ungrounded nickname cannot communicate a private unfamiliar name. Supply identifying semantic facts instead.
Never translate or transmit an external name letter by letter.

LOGICAL AND TEMPORAL COMPOSITION
Logical predicates take proposition arguments.
For if, ACTOR is the condition proposition and THEME is the consequence proposition.
For because, ACTOR is the result proposition and THEME is the reason proposition.
For before, ACTOR is the earlier event proposition and THEME is the later event proposition.
For after, ACTOR is the later event proposition and THEME is the earlier event proposition.
For and, both propositions hold. For inclusive or, at least one holds. Either-but-not-both excludes their both holding.
For consequence/then and therefore, ACTOR is the premise or condition and THEME is the consequence.
Unless relates ACTOR as the exceptional condition to THEME as the proposition that holds when that condition does not hold.
For unary temporal or modal predicates, THEME is the modified proposition.
Clause scope is lexical and explicit; no English word-order convention supplies missing boundaries.
Use report with ACTOR as original speaker and THEME as proposition, while retaining the actual sender's structural table.
To discuss a previous claim, use vu only if uniquely salient; otherwise bind its whole clause to a handle.
Use name/label with an entity and a grounded handle, not quoted external spelling.

EXACT COUNTS AND QUANTIFICATION
bo QUANTIFIER NUMBER bi CLAUSE lu ke is a complete sentence asserting a bound on the number of ALL distinct entities satisfying CLAUSE.
ne is bound to each entity being considered.
QUANTIFIER is x4vo exactly, xy2m at least, x8sc at most, x3hk more than, or xd6p less than.
NUMBER must be one directly listed cardinal quantity.
In this construction, bi introduces a restriction over potentially many entities, NOT a unique-entity description. Uniqueness is not required.
This construction constrains the entire matching set, never an arbitrary subset.
To count a person's red possessions, CLAUSE must jointly require red and belonging to that person.
This is a semantic quantifier, not a procedure for encoding or calculating a number.
A complete bo sentence may also be a proposition argument.
To negate or question a count, use an ordinary negated or question clause with zif as predicate and the whole bo sentence as THEME.

xafu all/every, xeb7 some, and x9wi none may be used as predicates with ACTOR a bi restriction and THEME a proposition containing ne.
All means every entity satisfying the restriction satisfies THEME; some means at least one does; none means no entity does.
Here the ACTOR bi supplies a potentially nonunique restriction over all matches, overriding ordinary bi uniqueness.
ne in THEME refers to each quantified entity, and its binding continues through nested proposition clauses.
Avoid nested entity descriptions in this construction; bind other referents first.
Do not use an ordinary unique description to imply an unexpressed exact count.

REFERENCE AND RELATIONAL WORDS
nra self/sender; npe addressee; ngi all participants; nqo other; ntu current salient referent; nha previously mentioned referent.
nmi current proposal; nwe previous claim; nna task-given context; n0e immediately preceding message.
nvi unknown queried entity; nio unknown queried place; n6a unknown queried quantity; nzo unknown queried reason; nbu unknown queried method; nus unknown queried time; n9a unknown queried truth value.
n2e identical entity; n7i possess/have; nya belong-to/be-of; neo have-property; noa be-instance/member-of.
naj greater-than; nle less-than; n3a earlier-than; ndo later-than.
For n7i, ACTOR possesses THEME. For nya, ACTOR belongs to THEME.
For neo, ACTOR has THEME property. For noa, ACTOR is an instance or member of THEME kind or set.
For comparisons, ACTOR is compared to THEME in the stated direction.
qyu has ordinal position: ACTOR entity, THEME directly listed ordinal.
qze has cardinal quantity: ACTOR collection, THEME directly listed cardinal quantity.
7uf is a synonym of qze with exactly the same roles.
jpa occupies task-visible position: ACTOR item, THEME grounded ordinal or location; ta may specify its containing list or grid.
zaj has color: ACTOR colored entity, THEME color value. Unary zta means ACTOR is red.

CARDINAL QUANTITIES
Each quantity is a complete lexical lookup. Adjacent quantity words do not form a larger numeral.
Unlisted exact values may be referred to through a task-visible entity bearing that value, not encoded as digits or decomposed into a calculation.
Use exact values, approximations, comparisons, or an honest unknown as appropriate.
Cardinal quantities and ordinal positions are different meanings.

jha possess/have; jme lack; jsa associated-with; jvi identical-referent; jno different-referent; jru complete; jfe incomplete.
For jha, ACTOR is the possessor and THEME is the possession. For jme, ACTOR lacks THEME.
For jic, ACTOR depends on THEME. For jux, ACTOR causes THEME. For jen, ACTOR prevents THEME. For jor, ACTOR is a prerequisite for THEME.

WORKED REFERENCE EXAMPLES
These examples explain the reference only. Never reproduce them as language lessons in task chat.
All examples assume agent_0 is the actual sender. Its structural row applies throughout, even when another agent is mentioned.

ha doq fo zra zta lu ke
This binds doq to the uniquely salient red item. The fo phrase combines item and red semantically.

ha dex bi falx qyu zavu ne kime qok ke lu ke
This binds dex to the unique entity in second ordinal position. Supply ta with a grounded list when needed to make the position unique.

ha dum bi falx vafu zavu falx zta zavu ne ke kime falx nya zavu ne kime agent_2 ke ke lu ke
This binds dum to the unique red entity belonging to agent_2.
Both ne arguments belong to the same bi, although they occur in separate proposition arguments of and.

falx v4vo zavu falx 7qu zavu agent_1 kime doq ke kime falx 7qu zavu me kime dex ke ke
If agent_1 chooses doq, I choose dex.
The outer ACTOR is the condition proposition and the outer THEME is the consequence proposition.
Both handles must already be grounded.

bo x4vo q4vo bi falx vafu zavu falx zta zavu ne ke kime falx nya zavu ne kime agent_2 ke ke lu ke
Exactly three entities are red and belong to agent_2.
This counts ALL matches; it does not identify three of possibly more matches.
The bi here is a counting restriction and does not require uniqueness.

rupq 7qu zavu agent_1 kime nvi ke
Which entity does agent_1 choose?
With no unknown argument, question mood instead requests a yes/no judgment.

USE AND REPAIR
Express essential facts first, then coordination and questions.
Use precise explicit roles and grounded handles when mistakes would affect the task.
A property can be predicated of an object. A proposition can be believed, negated, requested, compared, or assigned a confidence.
Never confuse content zax with question mood, zur with assertion mood, or zev correct with spatial zoi right.
When information is private, identify its owner or source with pu or so and predicate zahm. When it becomes shared, state zux or send/share it.
Different claims may be reported without endorsing them. Use nested report or believe clauses to preserve that distinction.
For a proposed plan, assert a preference or commitment toward a nested action clause.
For acceptance or refusal, use agree/disagree or deny with a clearly referenced proposal.
For correction, identify the mistaken claim and provide its replacement. Do not merely send an unexplained negation.
Clarify through semantic descriptions and grounded handles only.
Finish by reporting completion or remaining uncertainty, not by explaining the language.
Unknown exact names or numerical values must not be represented by spelling, positional digits, Unicode, ASCII, arithmetic, or any other calculated code.
